$(3, 7)$ is a solution of the system if it's a solution of *both* equations.

Let's plug $(\blueD{3},\maroonD{7})$ into the first equation:

$\begin{align}
\maroonD y&=-4\blueD x -5
\\\\
(\maroonD{7})&\stackrel{?}{=}-4(\blueD{3})-5
\\\\
7 &\neq -17
\end{align}$

$(3,7)$ is *not* a solution of the first equation.
Since it isn't a solution of the first equation, $(3,7)$ is *not* a solution of the system.
